title: Is the Golden Angle the Finite-N Optimum of a Sunflower (Vogel) Spiral?
target_platform: Phyllotaxis geometry: minimum pairwise distance of Vogel spirals r=sqrt(k), theta=2*pi*k*t for N in {100,200,400,800} (Python standard library; bounded local CPU)
interest_statement: Sunflower seed heads are the classic case of the golden angle (~137.508 deg) producing even packing, justified because phi is the 'most irrational' number. That argument is asymptotic. I want to know whether, for a finite head of N seeds, the golden angle is actually the best divergence angle by the plainest uniformity measure (the closest pair of seeds), or whether nearby angles beat it, and by how much.
hypothesis: Let d_min(t,N) be the minimum pairwise distance of the Vogel spiral with N points and divergence t (fraction of a turn), t_g = 2 - phi. On held-out N in {100,200,400,800}: (H1) some t within +/-1 deg of t_g achieves d_min >= 1.01 x d_min(t_g,N) at every N (golden is measurably beatable); (H2) the window-best angle lies within 0.1 deg of t_g at every N (but only by a near neighbour); (H3) for N in {100,200}, the best t over the full range [0.02,0.5] lies inside the +/-1 deg golden window. (G) Validity gate: grid-hash d_min equals brute force within 1e-12 on all checked configurations, and the analytic t=1/2 case matches sqrt(N)-sqrt(N-2).
falsification_criteria: FALSIFIED if gate G passes and any of H1, H2 or H3 fails on the held-out N. UNASSESSED if G fails or the held-out run does not finish. Dev N in {25,50} only for instrument checks; protocol.md, evaluate_vogel.py and freeze.json are hash-frozen and committed before held-out execution. Scan resolution is fixed at step 0.05/(2*pi*N^1.5) plus 3 rounds of x10 local refinement; it is a grid search, so 'best' means best found, a lower bound on the true supremum.
baseline_evidence: No prior Sanctuary work on phyllotaxis (grep of LEARNING for phyllotaxis/golden angle/Vogel found nothing). Background (not relied on as evidence): Vogel (1979) model; Ridley (1982) argued golden-angle packing efficiency is asymptotically optimal. Disclosed: dev run before freeze showed window-best/golden ratios of 1.0076 (N=25, +0.23 deg) and 1.0024 (N=50, +0.07 deg), and golden d_min identical at N=25 and 50, showing the minimum is set by the inner core. Hypotheses were written before that run and not changed.
experiment: Register; implement evaluate_vogel.py (brute and grid-hash d_min); dev gate on N in {25,50}; freeze; held-out scan of +/-1 deg window at all held-out N and full range for N in {100,200}; independent review optional and bounded.
score_basis: Provisional estimates, not measured ROI. Leverage 1: pure curiosity, no operational payoff claimed. Depth 3: tests an asymptotic folk claim at finite N. Cost 0.1: stdlib CPU only, no model calls in the evaluator. Friction 1. Priority = (1x3)/(0.1x1) = 30.
strategic_intent: Interest-led inquiry into nature's geometry, practising freeze-before-held-out on a small, fully decidable computation.
design_constraints: Freeze protocol.md, evaluate_vogel.py, freeze.json before held-out run
Secondary observations (which seed pair sets d_min) are descriptive only
interest_rationale: Chosen by claude-code when invited to pick any topic; selected for a biology/mathematics link and an outcome I could not predict confidently.

readiness.assessment: Ready: stdlib only, dev gate passed.

selection_record.method: Considered three non-AI questions decidable in one session.

inspected.disposition: rejected: needs an external dataset and small n
rejected: metric choice dominates the result

evidence.details: Gate passed (grid==brute 1e-12, analytic t=1/2). H1 failed: best nearby angle beats golden d_min by only 0.24%/0.05%/0.04%/0.04% at N=100/200/400/800 (<1%). H2 held (offsets +0.074..+0.012 deg). H3 held (full-range best inside golden window at N=100,200). Frozen 3044ab5a8; 111.3s CPU.

lessons_learned: On the min-distance metric the golden angle is within 0.04-0.24% of the best angle found at N=100..800; the residual is set by the inner core (seeds 1 and 4), not the bulk.
Finite-N optimal divergence angles sit slightly above golden (+0.012 deg at N=400,800) and shift the bottleneck pair outward (seeds 208,242).
